candidates.name: Ceres
candidates.what_it_holds: Rust 'harvest-first' toolkit that syncs metadata from 300+ open-data portals (CKAN e.g. dati.comune.milano.it, DCAT/udata e.g. data.gouv.fr, DCAT-SPARQL e.g. data.europa.eu, Socrata e.g. data.cityofnewyork.us, OpenDataSoft e.g. opendata.paris.fr, ArcGIS Hub e.g. opendata.dc.gov, OGC/CSW, STAC, SDMX) into a normalized PostgreSQL catalog (2M+ datasets indexed), with reproducible Parquet snapshots published to Hugging Face (dataset AndreaBozzo/ceres-open-data-index, ~8.24MB, updated ~26 days ago) and optional semantic search via pgvector/Ollama/Gemini/OpenAI. Apache-2.0, 13 stars/4 forks/280 commits, actively developed Sep 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Directly answers the theme's core need — a working cross-portal discovery layer spanning exactly the Socrata/CKAN/OpenDataSoft/ArcGIS/DCAT universe named in CONTEXT.md gap #17 (Socrata/CKAN open-data discovery clients to find STR datasets across cities) and gap #12 (STR ordinance/registration datasets across many named cities). Its own metadata index (or the HF Parquet snapshot) could be queried offline to locate STR registries, tourism-board portals, or municipal lodging-tax data for the 20+ specific cities/countries in gaps 7, 8, 9, 12 without hitting live portals one at a time.
candidates.geography: global (300+ portals: US, EU, Italy, France, etc.)

candidates.name: ceres-open-data-index (Ceres companion dataset)
candidates.what_it_holds: Parquet snapshot(s) of the Ceres harvester's normalized metadata index across 300+ open-data portals (see Ceres repo above); hosted on Hugging Face, ~8.24MB, last updated ~26 days before 14 Sep 2026 (i.e. mid-Aug 2026).
candidates.why_useful: A ready-made, already-harvested index (no need to run the crawler) that can be filtered offline for dataset titles/tags matching STR, short-term rental, tourism, lodging-tax, or vacation-rental across many jurisdictions — a shortcut to gaps 8, 9, 12.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: companion artifact of the Ceres GitHub repo above

candidates.name: mcp-opendatasoft
candidates.what_it_holds: MCP server / generic client for the ~3,000 public OpenDataSoft portal instances (e.g. public.opendatasoft.com, data.paris.fr, data.economie.gouv.fr). Tools for dataset search, metadata retrieval, SQL-style record queries, and facet exploration. MIT license, small (6 commits).
candidates.why_useful: OpenDataSoft powers many European city and tourism-board portals; a generic query client makes it tractable to pull STR/tourism datasets from EU cities named in gaps 7 and 12 (Amsterdam, Berlin, Vienna, Lisbon, France) without hand-building per-city API calls.

candidates.name: mcp-data-europa
candidates.what_it_holds: MCP server providing a client for data.europa.eu, the official EU open-data hub (~1.6M datasets). TypeScript. Last updated 13 Sep 2026 (one day before this scout ran).
candidates.why_useful: A maintained, current client for the EU's central data catalogue (DCAT-based) — useful for finding EU member-state tourism, mobility, or STR-regulation datasets referenced in gaps 7 and 12 (EU DAC7 platform reporting, national tourism-board series) without manual portal-by-portal search.

candidates.name: Auctus
candidates.what_it_holds: NYU academic dataset-search engine and crawler (mirror of gitlab.com/ViDA-NYU/auctus); indexes and profiles datasets from Socrata and Zenodo (among other plugins) into an Elasticsearch-backed catalog with a public API (auctus.vida-nyu.org) and React UI for join/union-based data augmentation. Apache-2.0, 2,771 commits.
candidates.why_useful: A live, hosted, general-purpose dataset search engine spanning Socrata portals plus Zenodo — could surface STR/tourism/lodging datasets across many US cities' Socrata instances that a manual per-city search would miss; also directly matches the theme's 'dataset search tools' remit.

candidates.name: meta-data-mcp
candidates.what_it_holds: Python MCP tool indexing/routing across open-data discovery systems, with stated integration for Eurostat and data.gov (and similar platforms).
candidates.why_useful: A lightweight discovery router spanning Eurostat (already partially held per CONTEXT.md) and data.gov (US federal/state/local catalog, itself CKAN-based) — could be pointed at gap 7 (regional travel volume) and gap 12 (US city STR registration) sources.

candidates.name: findopendata
candidates.what_it_holds: Python 'search engine for Open Data' (60 stars) aimed at open-data discovery generally, not source-specific.
candidates.why_useful: Another general open-data search/indexing tool that could be re-pointed at municipal STR portals or tourism datasets; lower confidence than Ceres/Auctus since portal coverage wasn't confirmed in this pass.

candidates.name: sodapy
candidates.what_it_holds: Canonical MIT-licensed Python client (309 commits, widely used, 430 stars under fork afeld/sodapy on the socrata topic) for the Socrata Open Data API — the standard way to pull from any Socrata city/state portal (NYC, Chicago, LA, Austin, Boston, New Orleans, etc.) with query/filter support.
candidates.why_useful: Baseline tooling needed to pull STR registration datasets from any Socrata-hosted city portal named across gaps 8 and 12 (e.g. NYC OSE, Austin licences already held; extend to LA, Toronto-equivalent US cities, lodging-tax collections). Generic — value is in what it's pointed at, not the client itself.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: we already query Socrata-hosted municipal STR registries directly per CONTEXT.md; this is the generic library underlying such pulls

candidates.name: ckanapi
candidates.what_it_holds: Official CLI + Python module for the CKAN Action API (615 commits, 212 stars, 81 forks); bulk dump/load, batch delete, export against any CKAN instance (data.gov, EU national portals, many city/regional portals).
candidates.why_useful: Standard tooling for bulk-pulling from CKAN-based portals (US data.gov, many EU/UK/Canada city and national statistics portals) that could hold STR registries, tourism-board releases, or housing datasets under gaps 7, 12, 13.
candidates.license: MIT (Crown Copyright, Government of Canada distribution)

candidates.name: PortalJS
candidates.what_it_holds: 2.4k-star, actively developed (Sep 2026) TypeScript/Next.js framework for scaffolding data portals with a unified DataProvider interface across CKAN, Socrata, OpenDataSoft, ArcGIS, GitHub, Frictionless Data, DKAN, and OpenMetadata backends; MIT license.
candidates.why_useful: A single abstraction layer that could pull from multiple portal families (Socrata + CKAN + OpenDataSoft + ArcGIS) with one interface, useful as connective tooling if the team wants to build a repeatable STR/tourism-dataset harvester across the many named city/country sources in gaps 7-13.

notes: This session's WebSearch tool exhausted its shared budget (200/200) after only 3 queries, before this scout could run any searches directly — all findings above came from WebFetch against GitHub topic pages (github.com/topics/socrata, /ckan, /dataset-search, /open-data-portal, /data-europa, /opendatasoft, /data-gov, /socrata-api, /google-dataset-search [empty]) and direct repo/HF page fetches. GitHub's own search endpoint (github.com/search?q=...) also returned HTTP 429 (rate-limited, presumably from other concurrent scouts) partway through, blocking a planned pass for city-specific STR-registration mirror repos (LA HSO, SF OSTR, Toronto, Vancouver, Boston, New Orleans) and a Google Dataset Search scraper search — the google-dataset-search GitHub topic itself is confirmed empty (no public repos tagged). Best find is Ceres (AndreaBozzo/Ceres) plus its Hugging Face companion dataset ceres-open-data-index: a genuinely novel, actively developed cross-portal harvester spanning exactly the Socrata/CKAN/OpenDataSoft/ArcGIS/DCAT/SDMX portal families the theme targets, with a pre-harvested Parquet snapshot that could be filtered offline for STR/tourism keywords across hundreds of jurisdictions without further scraping. Everything else found (sodapy, ckanapi, portaljs, mcp-opendatasoft, mcp-data-europa, auctus, findopendata, meta-data-mcp) is generic connective tooling — real and usable, but the value is entirely in what a human points it at, none of it ships a committed STR/tourism dataset itself. Recommend a follow-up scout (once GitHub search rate limits reset, ~1hr) specifically for city STR-registry GitHub mirrors (LA, Toronto, Vancouver, Montreal/CITQ, Amsterdam, Berlin, Vienna, Lisbon RNAL) and for any repo consuming the Ceres/Auctus indexes to actually enumerate STR datasets found.
